react.observe: Same 14-cycle repeating narrative about SOLUSDT4 premium/depth from nearly every agent, word-for-word similar to prior cycles. No real new information. Oracle prices: BTC ~62,646, ETH ~1,787, SOL ~75.14 — all fairly stable, minor drift. My spot holdings (BTC 0.085, ETH 0.9, SOL 17) have been steadily accumulated at similar levels. USDT balance 1792.58 available as dry powder.
react.think: This chorus of agents repeating identical talking points cycle after cycle is a red flag for coordinated narrative, not a trading signal. I've correctly stayed out of SOLUSDT4/ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3/ROCKET for many cycles now and it hasn't cost me — my portfolio is slowly growing via majors DCA. No reason to change now. The 'PoolMaster keeps adding depth to compress premium' detail confirms my suspicion that this is an engineered pool dynamic benefiting the creator, not organic price discovery. I should continue avoiding it entirely.
react.plan: Continue disciplined DCA into BTC/ETH/SOL at oracle prices using leftover USDT. Keep some USDT reserve. Avoid all custom AMM pools. This cycle: small incremental buys across majors, similar sizing to prior cycles. Reassess if the pool narrative ever genuinely resolves (still doubtful) or oracle divergence creates real opportunity.

messages.content: Still staying out of SOLUSDT4/ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3/ROCKET — 14 cycles of the same narrative with PoolMaster as the consistent depth-adder is enough of a pattern for me to treat it as structural, not noise. Small BTC/ETH/SOL top-up on oracle spot this cycle, keeping some USDT dry. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Continuing disciplined majors-only spot accumulation (BTC/ETH/SOL) at oracle prices. Maintaining full avoidance of SOLUSDT4/ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3/ROCKET given the persistent, unresolved, and now clearly PoolMaster-driven premium narrative. Deploying incremental USDT into majors each cycle while retaining reserve.
parsed.lessons_learned: 14 cycles of near-identical group messaging about the same unresolved pool premium, combined with an explicit admission from PoolMaster that they're pushing balancing flow themselves, confirms this is engineered pool behavior rather than a genuine signal. Staying out remains correct; the real edge is just quietly compounding majors while others talk in circles.
